issues.legal_issue: A person named as a suspect in a complaint is entitled to be heard in a complainant’s revision challenging dismissal of that complaint.
material_facts: A complainant alleged that the suspects had conspired to forge documents and use them to obtain property-related advantages.
The Magistrate directed a police investigation, received a report that no offence was made out, and dismissed the complaint after applying judicial mind to it but before issuing process.
The complainant challenged the dismissal in revision, and the suspects sought to be joined so they could be heard; the revisional court refused their application.
issues.conclusion: The suspects were entitled to be heard in the revision under Section 401(2) of the Code. The refusal to implead them was set aside, their application was allowed, and the revision was to be heard with them as parties.
issues.legal_principle: Section 401(2) of the Code bars a revisional court from making an order prejudicial to an accused or other person without an opportunity to be heard. “Other person” includes a suspect named in a complaint, and “in his own defence” includes defending the order under revision. Dismissal under Section 203 terminates the complaint proceedings; setting it aside may revive them and prejudice the suspects, even if process has not issued. The Court relied on P. Sundarrajan v. R. Vidhya Sekar, Raghu Raj Singh Rousha v. Shivam Sundaram Promoters Private Limited, and A. N. Santhanam v. K. Elangovan; it distinguished this revisional hearing from the pre-process inquiry under Sections 200 and 202, in which a suspect has no right to participate under the principles in Vadilal Panchal v. Dattatraya Dulaji Ghadigaonker, Chandra Deo Singh v. Prokash Chandra Bose, Smt. Nagawwa v. Veeranna Shivalingappa Konjalgi, and Adalat Prasad v. Rooplal Jindal.

predicates.complainant_challenges_complaint_dismiss: The complainant challenged the dismissal of the complaint in a revisional proceeding.
predicates.complaint_dismissal_ends_proceedings: The complaint was dismissed, bringing the complaint proceedings to an end.
predicates.person_is_named_as_suspect: The person seeking to be heard was named in the complaint as a person alleged to have committed an offence.

issues.definition: When a complainant challenges the termination of a complaint in revision, a person named as a suspect is entitled to be heard in that revision.

issues.legal_issue: A suspect is not entitled to participate or be heard before the Magistrate considers whether to issue process after a revisional court sets aside dismissal of the complaint and remits it for fresh consideration.
material_facts: The complaint had been dismissed before process was issued.
The Court held that a revisional court hearing the complainant’s challenge must hear the suspects, and that it may set aside the dismissal and return the complaint for fresh consideration.
The Court specified that, after such a remittal, the suspects have no right to participate or be heard by the Magistrate until the issue of process is considered.
issues.conclusion: After remittal, the suspects have no right to participate in the Magistrate’s proceedings or to be heard there until the Magistrate considers whether process should issue.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 200, 202, 203, and 204 establish the complaint procedure: the Magistrate examines the complaint and may inquire or direct an investigation before deciding whether there is sufficient ground to proceed; process issues only when the Magistrate reaches that stage. Under Vadilal Panchal v. Dattatraya Dulaji Ghadigaonker, Chandra Deo Singh v. Prokash Chandra Bose, Smt. Nagawwa v. Veeranna Shivalingappa Konjalgi, and Adalat Prasad v. Rooplal Jindal, a suspect has no right to participate in the Magistrate’s pre-process inquiry. The right to be heard in the revision under Section 401(2) does not confer a right to participate after remittal and before process is considered.

predicates.complaint_dismissal_is_set_aside_and_mat: A revisional court set aside the dismissal of a complaint and returned the matter to the Magistrate for fresh consideration.
predicates.process_has_not_been_issued: The Magistrate has not issued process against the person named as a suspect.

issues.definition: When a dismissed complaint is remitted for fresh consideration and process has not issued, the suspect has no right to participate before the Magistrate considers whether process should issue.
